statement: When the official Problem C statement is unavailable, reconstruct only deliverables explicitly evidenced by the paper, label the context gap, preserve filename/path classification, and do not claim official-requirement coverage.
applicability: Missing or incomplete official task context
inapplicable: Cases with a verified complete official problem statement
procedure: Search the manifest and context inventory for an authoritative statement.
Record exactly which official documents are present and absent.
Keep the A-F type as a pure function of filename and parent path.
Extract objectives and deliverables only from explicit paper restatements and summary claims.
Mark each reconstructed item as paper-implied rather than official.
Evaluate internal coherence and paper-implied coverage separately from official coverage.
Add the missing statement to unresolved questions and revisit if authoritative context appears.
positive_pattern: The paper is classified C from C-6947-Outstanding.pdf; its marine-risk and policy objectives are described as paper-implied, while official 2010 Problem C coverage remains unknown.
forbidden: Inferring problem type from subject matter
Inventing official deliverables
Treating an absent statement as fully reconstructed
Using a different problem statement because it seems related
Silently omitting the context limitation

statement: Convert every consequential Problem C assumption into a scoped, testable claim with a violation consequence, diagnostic, sensitivity range, uncertainty contribution, and non-use condition; convenience or measurement difficulty never establishes truth or zero effect.
inapplicable: Pure definitions that do not affect outputs
procedure: List each assumption beside the equation, data step, model, or decision it enables.
Classify it as structural, behavioral, sampling, measurement, temporal, causal, or decision-related.
State excluded mechanisms, entities, regimes, and failure consequences.
Define observable diagnostics, backtests, or external evidence that would support or reject it.
Replace point assumptions with ranges, scenarios, hierarchical effects, or omitted-variable bounds where possible.
Propagate assumption uncertainty to results, ranks, intervals, and decisions.
Declare deployment contexts in which violations suppress model use.
positive_pattern: A fixed future roster, uniform species behavior, stable history, and zero residual are each treated as explicit scenarios; the report shows how violations change outputs and when recommendations are withheld.
forbidden: Difficult to measure therefore negligible
Official data therefore error-free
Necessary assumption presented as truth
A limitation paragraph with no output consequence
Universal behavior imposed on heterogeneous populations
Future entities copied from the present without scenarios
Residual set to zero to create an effect
No sensitivity or non-use condition

statement: Establish environmental-data provenance, sampling design, representativeness, units, interval semantics, detection process, and uncertainty before generalizing a Problem C estimate across space, time, taxa, or policy contexts.
inapplicable: Fully synthetic demonstrations explicitly making no empirical claim
procedure: Record source, date, geography, population, sampling frame, effort, instrument, detection rules, exclusions, and units.
Map spatial, temporal, taxonomic, and environmental coverage against the target population.
Preserve intervals and censoring rather than replacing bins with arbitrary endpoints.
Estimate sampling, measurement, detection, and preprocessing uncertainty.
Compare the sample with independent surveys or known population margins.
Use stratification, weighting, hierarchical models, or restricted claims to address coverage gaps.
Carry provenance and uncertainty into every result and figure.
positive_pattern: Mesh-bin counts retain interval bounds and survey effort, use interval-censored size distributions, and are combined across seasons and sites with design weights and confidence intervals.
forbidden: One sample called representative by assumption
Bin boundary used as exact size without sensitivity
Published point estimate with no source metadata
Trend lines combining incomparable surveys
Region-wide policy from unexamined local coverage
Units missing from charts

statement: Define data-validity and exclusion criteria independently and before outcome scoring; never discard observations merely because their scores are low, inconvenient, or inconsistent with the desired mechanism.
inapplicable: Post-analysis decision filtering that explicitly retains all data in estimation
procedure: Separate measurement validity, scope eligibility, and outcome magnitude.
Pre-register exclusion rules using instrument failure, duplication, protocol violation, or target-population mismatch.
Record every excluded item and reason before fitting or ranking.
Retain valid low-scoring cases and model alternative mechanisms they may represent.
Compare full-data and filtered results.
Run influence, deletion, and threshold sensitivity.
If selection depends on the outcome, model the selection process or qualify the estimate as selected-sample only.
positive_pattern: All mesh bins remain in the primary analysis; a predeclared ingestion-only secondary analysis is reported separately, and policy rankings are stress-tested against inclusion of large-debris entanglement harm.
forbidden: Low score means invalid data
Deleting cases after viewing the ranking
Using plausibility of the retained range as proof of accuracy
Removing a mechanism by filtering its observations
No exclusion ledger
No full-versus-filtered comparison

statement: Define the decision estimand, observational unit, prediction horizon, and outcome scale before modeling; keep occurrence, composition, classification, probability, count, severity, ordinal score, causal effect, utility, and management priority mathematically distinct.
applicability: All Problem C prediction, risk, ranking, causal, and policy models
inapplicable: Purely descriptive tables with an explicit unit and no inferential claim
procedure: Name the target population, unit, time cutoff, horizon, endpoint, conditioning set, and decision use.
Draw the source-to-observation-to-model-to-result chain.
Assign every dataset, row, feature, label, and aggregate to one semantic level.
Specify separate equations and units for probabilities, counts, rates, severities, ordinal outcomes, and utilities.
Validate intermediate models after aggregation at the official target.
Calibrate or identify the claimed endpoint, or restrict language to the measurable proxy.
Prevent summaries, figures, and recommendations from changing the estimand name.
positive_pattern: An athlete event-medal classifier is explicitly intermediate; event awards are allocated under rules, country gold and total counts are backtested, and a first-medal hazard uses NOC-Games transitions rather than a repeated ever-medaled label.
forbidden: Composition share called damage
Static historical status called future event probability
Athlete classification accuracy called country-count accuracy
Ordinal podium score called medal-count contribution
Composite index called observed harm
Switching endpoints between methods and conclusions
Undefined risk or capability

statement: Represent all material mechanisms and population heterogeneity capable of changing a Problem C environmental ranking, or bound and disclose the excluded mechanisms before policy use.
inapplicable: Narrow studies explicitly limited to one validated mechanism and endpoint
procedure: Enumerate ingestion, entanglement, toxicity, abrasion, transport, persistence, biofouling, habitat, and other domain-relevant mechanisms.
Map which materials, sizes, taxa, life stages, and environments activate each mechanism.
Use stratified, hierarchical, mixture, or multi-endpoint models instead of universal behavior when data permit.
Estimate interactions between abundance, size, shape, chemistry, behavior, and exposure.
For unavailable mechanisms, construct literature-supported bounds and scenario weights.
Report mechanism-specific and aggregate rankings.
Suppress universal policy rankings when omitted mechanisms can reverse decisions.
positive_pattern: Material rankings combine taxon-specific ingestion, entanglement, and toxicity endpoints with bounded missing data; the report shows when each mechanism controls the decision.
forbidden: Ingestion-only ranking called total harm
Same behavior for all species
Piece count as the sole damage function
Outcome-based deletion of large debris
Difficult variable assigned zero effect
No reversal analysis

statement: Treat multi-criteria weights as evidence-bearing preferences or calibrated parameters, document their provenance, and report decision stability across plausible weights and aggregation choices.
inapplicable: Single-criterion decisions with no hidden scalarization
procedure: Define each criterion, direction, scale, overlap, and stakeholder meaning.
Choose empirical calibration, structured expert elicitation, stakeholder elicitation, or a declared normative basis.
Record participants, method, consistency, uncertainty, and conflicts.
Normalize criteria with justified value functions rather than arbitrary scale convenience.
Sweep continuous weights and alternative aggregation families.
Compute rank acceptability, switch thresholds, and robust or dominated options.
Keep hard ecological constraints outside compensatory weighting when substitution is unacceptable.
positive_pattern: Abundance and size weights come from documented expert/stakeholder elicitation, and an interval analysis shows the precise weight ranges where the recommended material changes.
forbidden: Common sense as weight evidence
Ordinal rank presented as causal importance
One weight vector only
No rank-switch analysis
Double-counted criteria
Small ecological weight allowed to erase a critical limit

statement: Run a formula-to-output preflight for every Problem C transformation: preserve data semantics, verify units and invariants, reproduce intermediate values and worked examples, and reconcile equations, code, tables, figures, and prose before interpretation.
applicability: All equation, count, normalization, regression, matrix, simulation, and aggregation models
procedure: Create a symbol and data-grain table with units, domains, cutoffs, and transformation state.
State why each normalization, link, score, average, ratio, or value function matches its meaning.
Hand-calculate small fixtures and each headline intermediate result.
Check sums, bounds, monotonicity, limiting cases, event-count limits, matrix dimensions, and arithmetic identities.
Recompute regression exponent interpretations and interval/point consistency.
Compare printed equations, implementation, tables, figures, and narrative labels.
Automate invariants and fail the pipeline on disagreement.
Interpret the aggregate only at the weakest semantic level supported by its inputs.
positive_pattern: Tests catch a denominator typo, conflicting coefficients, a wrong exponent, an impossible event medal count, and a wrong coach-effect average before any result enters the summary.
forbidden: Equation and result using different denominators
Two coefficients for one fitted model
Exponent that does not match the percentage
Worked-example average without recalculation
Athlete-row total exceeding event award bounds
Point estimate unexplained at an interval boundary
Arithmetic consistency treated as empirical validity

statement: Propagate sampling, measurement, preprocessing, parameter, calibration, entity-population, scenario, structural, weight, and threshold uncertainty through Problem C outputs and decisions; distinguish conditional outcome randomness from full predictive uncertainty.
inapplicable: Deterministic identities with exact inputs and no decision claim
procedure: List every uncertain input, entity set, model component, and structural choice.
Estimate sampling and parameter distributions or defensible bounds.
Vary preprocessing, inclusion, calibration, future entities, program/scenario inputs, weights, mechanisms, and thresholds.
Nest conditional outcome simulation inside parameter, model, and scenario draws when needed.
Recompute official outputs and decisions for each draw.
Report intervals, coverage, rank probabilities, switch surfaces, and regret by uncertainty source.
Identify dominant uncertainty and collect data where decisions are sensitive.
positive_pattern: Medal intervals vary fitted models, probability calibration, 2028 rosters, event programs, and structural assumptions before drawing event outcomes; ecological rankings likewise vary sampling, bins, mechanisms, and weights.
forbidden: Fixed-probability draws called model uncertainty
Point ranking without intervals
Recall mislabeled sensitivity analysis
Future roster copied without a scenario
Subjective weights held fixed
Selection uncertainty ignored
No decision-switch analysis

statement: Validate a Problem C model against independent data at the declared target, time horizon, aggregation level, and deployment population before claiming accuracy, causality, generality, or transferability.
inapplicable: Exploratory descriptive indices explicitly making no predictive or transfer claim
procedure: Select validation targets that exactly match the declared estimand.
Hold out future periods, locations, taxa, entities, or surveys before development.
Group repeated entities so no identity crosses incompatible splits.
Run the complete preprocessing, model, constraint, and aggregation pipeline in each fold.
Compare with simple, mechanistic, and local baselines.
Evaluate calibration, count error, interval coverage, ranking, subgroup error, and decision utility as appropriate.
Use influence and specification tests as supplements rather than substitutes.
Report failure conditions and restrict claims to validated domains.
positive_pattern: Olympic models roll through historical cutoffs and score held-out country gold and total counts with coverage; environmental risk models test independent biological endpoints across taxa, regions, and years.
forbidden: Random athlete-row accuracy called future country-count validation
Validation against an input used to build the score
Plausible inputs called accuracy
Same formula called transferability
One convenient sport used to validate all outputs
LOO or AIC treated as causal validation
No baseline

statement: Name each Problem C result by the operation and estimand that produced it; never convert a composition, classification, normalized score, expected count, regression association, or conditional simulation interval into observed harm, causal effect, or full prediction without corresponding evidence.
applicability: All modeled results, tables, captions, summaries, and recommendations
inapplicable: Direct design-based estimates whose attribution and uncertainty are fully established
procedure: Trace each headline result backward through data grain, labels, filters, transformations, models, and constraints.
State whether it is an observation, conditional composition, classification probability, count forecast, expected count, association, causal effect, utility, or score.
Keep units, cutoff, population, conditioning, and uncertainty scope visible.
Reconcile point estimates with quantiles and full-population coverage.
Separate arithmetic decomposition and regression association from causal attribution.
Use causal or endpoint language only after identification and validation.
Scan summaries, captions, recommendations, and memos for semantic escalation.
positive_pattern: A fixed-roster Monte Carlo interval is labeled conditional on calibrated probabilities and one event program; a coefficient remains an association until a causal design; a composition share remains a score-weighted composition.
forbidden: Score share caused the same share of damage
Static label probability called first-medal odds
Expected count from an invalid cohort
Regression coefficient called host or coach contribution
Conditional outcome draws called full uncertainty
Point estimate at an interval boundary with no explanation
Abstract stronger than methods

statement: Derive environmental policy tiers, thresholds, taxes, fines, targets, and mixture rules from explicit objectives, causal response, cost, feasibility, legal authority, distributional effects, and uncertainty; a relative score alone cannot set policy intensity.
inapplicable: Pure descriptive rankings with no policy recommendation
procedure: Define the decision maker, affected parties, legal scope, objective, constraints, and time horizon.
Estimate how each instrument changes behavior, exposure, harm, revenue, compliance, and substitution.
Model implementation and monitoring cost, administrative capacity, and incidence.
Choose thresholds through expected loss, cost-effectiveness, robust optimization, or documented stakeholder standards.
Test mixture rules at boundaries and under uncertainty.
Compare alternative instruments and a no-action baseline.
Report distributional, unintended, and ecological effects.
Attach review triggers and adaptive revision to uncertain thresholds.
positive_pattern: Reuse targets and fees are chosen from material-specific harm reduction and compliance curves under budget and equity constraints, with robust thresholds and scheduled reassessment.
forbidden: High score means highest tax
Round-number reuse target
Fine copied without legal or behavioral analysis
Post hoc high/middle/low classes
Ninety-percent mixture cutoff without loss model
No cost or feasibility
No uncertainty buffer

statement: Close the Problem C evidence-to-decision chain: every recommendation must trace to a modeled or separately cited mechanism, quantified result, uncertainty bound, decision criterion, implementation constraint, cost, and monitoring or review trigger.
inapplicable: Clearly labeled brainstorming with no recommendation
procedure: Create a requirement-to-analysis-to-result-to-action matrix.
For each action, name the mechanism and whether support comes from the model or external evidence.
Quantify expected benefit, harm, cost, timing, and uncertainty in the requested unit.
State feasibility, governance, legal, stakeholder, and data constraints.
Compare alternatives and no action.
Define indicators, baseline, trigger, stop or revision rule, and review schedule.
Remove or relabel recommendations lacking a complete trace.
Carry the same bounds and caveats into the summary and stakeholder communication.
positive_pattern: A coaching investment names the country-sport treatment, identified medal-count effect, interval, cost and opportunity cost, feasibility, competing investments, and post-hire evaluation trigger; an environmental action follows the same chain.
forbidden: Recommendation unrelated to modeled variables
Model-excluded factor presented as a model result
Three requested investments with only qualitative effects
Policy list with no amounts or costs
Broad advice from one static score
Regional stereotype used as a variable
No monitoring or revision
Effective or economic without metrics

statement: Use Problem C figures to expose data support, units, model structure, uncertainty, calibration, and decision stability with low-distortion encodings; captions and diagrams must not imply dynamics, causality, validation, or precision absent from the model.
inapplicable: No-figure outputs
procedure: Choose the chart from the analytical question and data type.
Label units, population, cutoff, conditioning, time, geography, and source.
Show raw observations or sample support where useful.
Display intervals, distributions, calibration, coverage, rank probabilities, or scenario bands.
Use sorted 2D dots/bars for categorical probabilities and reserve 3D for genuine spatial dimensions.
Make workflow arrows match implemented equations, time steps, and feedback.
Mark thresholds, selected decisions, alternatives, and switch regions.
Remove decorative repetitions when a precise chart already exists.
Reconcile every plotted value with reproducible outputs.
positive_pattern: A forecast dashboard combines all-country point/interval plots, calibration and rolling-error panels, and a scenario comparison; a ranked probability chart replaces a word cloud and every interval states its uncertainty scope.
forbidden: Perspective 3D categorical bars
Probability word cloud replacing a ranked chart
Trend without units or comparable sampling
Workflow called simulation without dynamics
ROC/PR used as final count validation
No uncertainty
Decorative chart replacing audit tables

statement: Calibrate Problem C language to the evidence class: distinguish assumption, arithmetic consistency, classification performance, calibration, association, prediction, conditional simulation, causal effect, accuracy, transferability, cost-effectiveness, and observed outcome in every section, including AI-assisted prose.
procedure: Tag each major claim by source and inferential level.
Use explicit subjects such as data show, model estimates, scenario assumes, regression associates, or external study reports.
Reserve accurate for evaluated error against the deployment target.
Reserve causal terms for identified effects and probability terms for calibrated probabilities.
Reserve transferable for tested out-of-domain performance.
Name the metric behind effective, economic, robust, representative, scientific, valid, and feasible.
Distinguish recall from sensitivity analysis and elasticity from a one-unit effect.
Independently check AI-polished claims against methods, code, and domain facts.
Run a semantic-escalation scan from methods to headlines.
positive_pattern: Conditional on a fixed 2024 roster, one program scenario, and calibrated probabilities, the simulation estimates a country-count interval; the report does not call it full uncertainty or proof of accuracy.
forbidden: Common sense as empirical evidence
Random-fold AUC proves future country counts
Recall called assumption sensitivity
Positive regression coefficient contributes causally
Plausible inputs confirm validity
Same formula means transferable
Score share caused damage
Scientific and feasible without metrics
AI fluency treated as verification

statement: Before recommending ecological cleanup or intervention, define the intervention mechanism, site-specific baseline, non-target risks, operational constraints, safeguards, monitoring, stop rules, and adaptive review.
inapplicable: Non-intervention descriptive analysis
procedure: Specify the debris, habitat, taxa, location, timing, and removal technology.
Measure baseline debris and non-target abundance over relevant cycles.
Estimate removal efficiency, bycatch, disturbance, emissions, displacement, and worker risk.
Compare timing and technology alternatives with no action.
Set exclusion zones, operating limits, trigger thresholds, and emergency stop rules.
Pilot at small scale and monitor target and non-target outcomes.
Adapt or terminate based on predeclared criteria.
Report residual uncertainty and governance responsibility.
positive_pattern: Night cleanup proceeds only after site-specific diel plankton surveys, gear-selectivity trials, protected-area exclusions, bycatch thresholds, a monitored pilot, and an enforceable stop rule.
forbidden: Night work from a generic plankton claim
Efficient and economic without metrics
No non-target monitoring
No pilot
No stop rule
Assuming removal always improves ecosystem state

statement: Define and enforce the statistical grain, keys, outcome ownership, and cross-file reconciliation contract before modeling; convert repeated entity rows to the official scoring unit and assert hard domain counting invariants.
inapplicable: Single-table data with one verified row per target unit
procedure: Write the observational unit and target unit for every table and model stage.
Define canonical keys, NOC/entity mappings, time cutoffs, team/relay handling, ties, and outcome ownership.
Reconcile outcome totals across athlete, event, country, and summary tables.
Resolve or log retroactive changes and conflicting source metadata.
Deduplicate to event-country-medal or the domain-equivalent scoring unit before aggregation.
Assert upper/lower count bounds and conservation identities from rules.
Test joins for one-to-one, one-to-many, and accidental multiplication.
Version the reconciliation decisions and rerun downstream artifacts after changes.
positive_pattern: Relay athlete rows map to one event-NOC medal; Samoa's retroactive silver is reconciled from medal_counts; program-year conflicts become explicit scenarios; all event award bounds pass before forecasting.
forbidden: Summing athlete medal rows as country medals
One team member equals one team award
Ever-medaled status from one inconsistent file
Forty-five golds from eighteen events
Join multiplication left unchecked
Data authenticity assumed instead of tested
Conflicting metadata silently resolved
Intervention year outside treatment tenure

statement: For future Problem C prediction, construct cutoff-safe features, split by time and repeated entity, run the complete aggregation pipeline in rolling-origin backtests, and model future entity and design turnover as scenarios rather than copying the present.
inapplicable: Contemporaneous classification with no future claim and no repeated entities
procedure: Choose forecast cutoff, horizon, target entities, and design state.
Generate every feature using only records available before each cutoff; aggregate same-period duplicate rows before lagging.
Group athletes, teams, NOCs, sites, or other repeated entities to prevent leakage.
Use rolling historical cutoffs and reserve the latest periods for final evaluation.
Run preprocessing, model fitting, calibration, constraints, and aggregation anew in each backtest.
Evaluate official aggregate targets as well as intermediate predictions.
Create attrition, newcomer, qualification, and future-design scenarios or explicit generative models.
Report performance decay and suppress extrapolation beyond tested support.
positive_pattern: Train through 2012, predict 2016 with only pre-2016 features and a modeled roster, repeat through 2024, then forecast 2028 under multiple roster and program scenarios with country-count metrics.
forbidden: Random row split for a future forecast
Same athlete or NOC in train and test through identity features
Current-Games result entering another same-Games lag
2024 roster copied as 2028 without scenarios
Tree Year feature treated as extrapolation
One intermediate sport used to validate final totals
One-model-per-sport and per-event used interchangeably

statement: Model a first occurrence as a transition among units demonstrably at risk at a fixed cutoff; use one row per unit-period, cutoff-safe covariates, rare-event calibration, and rolling cohort validation before reporting unit odds or expected counts.
inapplicable: Repeated events where prior occurrence does not remove the unit from risk
procedure: Reconcile authoritative history and define the at-risk cohort at each cutoff.
Create one unit-period row and label whether the first event occurs in the next horizon.
Remove units from risk after their first event and resolve identity changes.
Use only covariates known at the cutoff and avoid repeated static ever/never labels.
Fit a discrete-time hazard, hierarchical rare-event, survival, or calibrated transition model with partial pooling.
Validate calibration, precision-recall, Brier/log score, expected count, and cohort coverage by rolling origin.
Compute expected event count as the sum of valid unit probabilities and simulate joint constraints when outcomes compete.
Report odds, uncertainty, and sensitivity to cohort reconciliation.
positive_pattern: Each NOC without a medal through year t contributes one row for Games t+1; Samoa is excluded after its reconciled 2008 silver, and 2028 probabilities are calibrated on prior first-medal transitions.
forbidden: Static ever-medaled label repeated across athlete rows
One-hot NOC memorization under random split
Already successful unit kept in the at-risk cohort
Athlete probability reused as country first-event probability
Expected count from invalid membership
Only present participants allowed to be future first movers
No calibration under class imbalance

statement: Before probability-driven simulation, calibrate out-of-fold probabilities, encode domain constraints and dependence, decompose uncertainty sources, and verify point, interval, and coverage consistency on historical backtests.
inapplicable: Exact deterministic calculations with no probability or interval claim
procedure: Generate predictions out of fold using time/entity-safe splits.
Assess reliability, Brier/log score, and subgroup calibration; recalibrate without reusing evaluation labels.
Define the sample space, award/resource constraints, ties, teams, quotas, and dependencies.
Separate aleatory outcome draws from parameter, calibration, model, entity-set, and scenario draws.
Use nested simulation or model ensembles to combine sources.
Backtest point error, empirical interval coverage, width, and decision performance across historical cutoffs.
Reconcile central estimates with quantiles and publish all requested intervals.
Fix seeds for reproducibility while varying seeds to assess Monte Carlo error.
positive_pattern: Calibrated historical cutoff predictions feed event-rule-aware simulations nested within roster, program, and model draws; held-out Games show near-nominal all-country coverage and coherent point/quantile summaries.
forbidden: Uncalibrated probability used as a sampling weight after known bias
Fixed fitted probabilities called model uncertainty
Generic three-winner rule for every event
Only top countries receive required intervals
Deterministic point equals an upper quantile without explanation
No backtested coverage
Simulation count chosen without Monte Carlo error check

statement: When a Problem C count changes with available opportunities, model the correctly deduplicated rate, share, or count with explicit exposure and time structure; do not interpret the mechanical increase in opportunities as a performance effect.
inapplicable: Counts with fixed opportunity and no time trend
procedure: Define and deduplicate the outcome at its scoring unit.
Measure the opportunity/exposure denominator and verify its units.
Decide whether the estimand is total count, rate per opportunity, share of awards, or marginal effect of changing opportunities.
Use offsets or joint binomial/multinomial/count models as appropriate.
Account for time trends, serial correlation, country/sport effects, and bounded maximums.
Check overdispersion and zero inflation after fixing grain, not before.
Compare Poisson, Negative Binomial, hurdle/ZIP, and simpler rate baselines out of sample.
Interpret log-link coefficients and elasticities with exact calculus.
Use a causal design before calling opportunity changes contributions.
positive_pattern: Event-NOC medals are deduplicated, total medal opportunities enter as an offset, country share is modeled over time, and a counterfactual program change is separated from general historical growth.
forbidden: Athlete-row medals as country count
Raw count regressed on its number of opportunities without exposure logic
Positive coefficient treated as causal
Time trend omitted
Only early historical years with no rationale
Elasticity beta*x called a growing one-event effect
Alternative distributions used to excuse wrong grain
Impossible counts accepted

statement: Estimate host, coach, program, or other intervention effects with verified treatment timing, a credible comparison counterfactual, pre-treatment diagnostics, confounder control, uncertainty, and placebo or falsification tests before using causal language or investment advice.
inapplicable: Pure prediction that explicitly makes no causal or intervention recommendation
procedure: Define treatment, unit, start/end dates, exposure intensity, outcome, horizon, and causal estimand.
Verify treatment history from allowed or documented sources.
Construct comparable untreated units or a synthetic counterfactual.
Use panel fixed effects, event studies, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, interrupted time series, or another justified design.
Check pretrends, anticipation, spillovers, concurrent changes, serial dependence, and treatment selection.
Estimate effect intervals and heterogeneity by country, sport, and event.
Run placebo dates, placebo units, leave-one-out donors, and sensitivity to unmeasured confounding.
Translate effects to expected medal counts and investment decisions with cost and uncertainty.
positive_pattern: Coach arrival dates define event-study treatment; comparable teams form a donor pool; pretrends and placebo dates pass; host-program additions are modeled by sport-country alignment; three investments report causal effect intervals and costs.
forbidden: Current result minus prior-three ordinal mean equals coach effect
Residual set to zero
Post-tenure outcome credited to coach
Single host observation interpreted causally
Separate tiny country regressions with no controls
Total event count substituted for host-selected event type
Robust positive association called contribution
Recommendation from one anecdote

statement: Convert every official Problem C clause, data restriction, output population, precision requirement, and submission artifact into a machine-checkable coverage row and fail completion when any required row lacks evidence.
inapplicable: Open-ended tasks with no explicit deliverables or constraints
procedure: Parse the official statement into atomic deliverables, subquestions, allowed-data rules, units, populations, and file requirements.
Map each row to data, estimand, method, validation, result, figure/table, conclusion, and page.
Mark full, partial, unsupported, or blocked coverage with reasons.
Check quantitative words such as all, each, three, intervals, odds, and estimate literally.
Audit references, summary, contents, page limits, and AI report alongside model outputs.
Verify every external context claim and asset is cited and allowed.
Run a final completeness linter and refuse done status on missing rows.
Carry partial-coverage labels into the summary rather than hiding them.
positive_pattern: The matrix verifies all-country gold/total intervals, rolling performance metrics, a reconciled first-medal cohort, event-type counterfactuals, three quantified coach investments, original NOC insight, references, and AI disclosure.
forbidden: Top-nine intervals when all results are required
Three recommendations with only one quantified
Host total-events regression used for host-chosen event types
References omitted
Only-data-provided restriction ignored
AI report present but adopted claims unchecked
A partial answer described as complete
Page-limit artifacts not reconciled

statement: When generative AI assists Problem C framing, modeling, code, or prose, map each interaction to adopted artifacts and independently verify domain rules, data restrictions, equations, calculations, code, citations, and claim strength before submission.
inapplicable: Workflows with no generative-AI use
procedure: Record tool, model/version when known, date, prompt, output, and purpose.
Map each output to final sections, equations, model choices, code, figures, or rejected suggestions.
Check suggestions against the official allowed-data boundary and deliverables.
Verify domain facts and hard constraints from primary or supplied sources.
Recalculate mathematics and run tests on AI-influenced code and outputs.
Compare AI-polished claims with actual validation, limitations, and architecture.
Document accept, modify, or reject decisions and unresolved warnings.
Scan the final paper for copied falsehoods, contradictions, or untraceable AI language.
positive_pattern: A model-ideation prompt is linked to each adopted component, event award rules are verified from supplied data, tests catch a false medal-allocation claim, and strengths are rewritten to match rolling backtests.
forbidden: Prompt disclosure treated as verification
AI-generated domain rule copied into conclusions
Fluent strengths without method evidence
One model per sport silently changed to per event
Avoids overfitting asserted without temporal tests
Population or other disallowed variables adopted from generic advice
No prompt-to-artifact map
No record of rejected output
